# Semantic cache theory

For normalized embedding vectors $A$ and $B$, cosine similarity is the dot
product:

$$\text{similarity}(A, B) = A \cdot B$$

The active semantic tier uses FAISS `METRIC_INNER_PRODUCT`, which is equivalent
to cosine similarity after L2 normalization. A query hits when the best
unexpired entry in the same tenant/model/parameter namespace has similarity
greater than or equal to the configured threshold.

Threshold selection is an empirical precision/recall trade-off, not a universal
constant. The committed sweep uses 24 paraphrases, 12 unrelated negatives, and
12 hard negatives:

| Threshold | Paraphrase hit rate | Hard-negative false positives |
|---|---|---|
| 0.80 | 37.5% | 8.3% |
| 0.85 | 29.2% | 0% |
| 0.90 | 12.5% | 0% |
| 0.95 | 0% | 0% |

Source: `data/evidence/semantic_threshold_sweep.csv`, generated by
`benchmarks/semantic_threshold_sweep.py`. No production hit-rate or latency
claim is made here.
